title.en: Nuclear fission, chain reaction and nuclear fusion
The discovery of Hahn and Strassmann

text.en: In 1939 the German scientists Otto Hahn and Fritz Strassmann bombarded uranium with neutrons and were surprised to find that the nucleus split into two nearly equal parts and released a huge amount of energy. This was the discovery of nuclear fission.

Nuclear fission is the splitting of a heavy nucleus into two smaller nuclei of comparable mass, releasing a few neutrons and a large amount of energy.
For example, U-235 absorbs a neutron and splits into barium-141 and krypton-92 with three neutrons and about 200 MeV, or 3.2 times 10 to the power minus 11 joule, of energy.
A fissile material such as U-235 or plutonium-239 undergoes sustained fission on absorbing a neutron, whereas natural uranium is 99.28 percent U-238, which is not fissile.
The three neutrons from one fission can cause three more fissions, then nine, then twenty-seven, and this self-propagating process is called a chain reaction.
In a controlled chain reaction extra neutrons are absorbed so that only one neutron causes the next fission, and this is used in a nuclear reactor to produce power steadily.
In an uncontrolled chain reaction the neutrons multiply in a geometrical progression and release huge energy in a fraction of a second, which is the principle of the atom bomb.
Some neutrons leak out or are absorbed by non-fissionable material, so a minimum quantity called the critical mass is needed to sustain the chain reaction.
A mass below the critical mass is subcritical and above it is supercritical; an atom bomb joins two subcritical pieces to make a supercritical mass.
In nuclear fusion two lighter nuclei combine to form a heavier nucleus and release energy, as happens in the Sun and in the hydrogen bomb, but it needs extremely high temperature.
In nuclear physics energy is measured in electron volt, 1 eV = 1.602 times 10 to the power minus 19 joule, and 1 MeV is 10 to the power 6 eV.

problem.en: Find the energy in joule released in one fission if it is 200 MeV. Also, complete the nuclear reactions of an alpha decay of U-238 and a beta decay of P-32.

why.en: Matches the book value of 3.2 x 10^-11 J.

text.en: Alpha decay: mass number falls by 4 and atomic number by 2, so U-238 (Z = 92) becomes Th-234 (Z = 90) plus He-4.

why.en: Alpha particle is a helium nucleus.

text.en: Beta decay: mass number is unchanged and atomic number rises by 1, so P-32 (Z = 15) becomes S-32 (Z = 16) plus an electron.

prompt.en: Explain the difference between a controlled and an uncontrolled chain reaction with an example of each.

requiredIdeas.en: Controlled: only one neutron per fission continues the reaction, used in a nuclear reactor
Uncontrolled: neutrons multiply rapidly, used in an atom bomb
A critical mass of fissile material is needed

commonMisconceptions.en: Both release energy at the same slow rate
Fusion is a type of chain reaction

points.en: Fission splits a heavy nucleus; fusion joins light nuclei.
Chain reaction: 1, 3, 9, 27 neutrons; controlled in a reactor, uncontrolled in an atom bomb.
Critical mass is the least mass of fissile material that sustains the chain reaction.
1 eV = 1.602 x 10^-19 J; one fission gives about 200 MeV.
